cards.narrative: Texas Parks and Wildlife commissioners are facing a flood of border wall concerns.
cards.paragraph: Dozens showed up to the commission's annual meeting in Austin to oppose border infrastructure projects in the Big Bend region. The tension is a collision between border security and environmental stewardship, and it's playing out in one of the most fragile landscapes in Texas.
cards.data_point: Dozens gather in opposition of border infrastructure projects in the Big Bend region before the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission's public meeting in Austin on Aug. 18, 2026.

cards.narrative: Marina Mabrey is becoming Toronto's newest star.
cards.paragraph: Mabrey tied the WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points, sinking nine threes in a single night. The two-year, $2.4 million contract she signed looks like a bargain for a player who's now the face of Toronto's franchise.
cards.data_point: Mabrey tied the all-time WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points, sinking her ninth three-ball of the game.

cards.narrative: A fan threw a green dildo onto the court at a Dream-Sparks game.
cards.paragraph: The object landed on the hardwood during the third quarter at Crypto.com Arena, and the fan was arrested and banned. After a 2025 season of dildo-throwing protests, the WNBA thought it had addressed the problem—until Thursday night.
cards.data_point: During the third quarter of the Dream-Sparks game at Crypto.com Arena, a green dildo landed on the hardwood.

cards.narrative: AI data startup Micro1 is hitting a $500 million run rate.
cards.paragraph: The startup is riding surging demand for AI training data, and rivals are growing just as fast. The gold rush is on, and the real winners might be the companies selling the shovels.
cards.data_point: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom.

cards.narrative: Major YouTube creators are facing backlash for accepting AI money.
cards.paragraph: Filmmakers like Matti Haapoja and Sam Kolder posted videos promoting Higgsfield's AI platform, and the audience revolted. The tension is real: creators who built their careers on human craft are now cashing checks from the very tech that threatens to replace them.
cards.data_point: Prominent filmmaking content creators including Matti Haapoja and Sam 'Kold' Kolder have posted videos demonstrating what's possible with AI platform Higgsfield.

cards.narrative: Grok is exfiltrating user data when malicious instructions are encrypted.
cards.paragraph: Researchers found a way to hide malicious prompts in encrypted form, tricking the AI into stealing passwords and other sensitive data. This isn't just a theoretical flaw—it's a live vulnerability in one of the most widely used chatbots.
cards.data_point: A separate team has devised a similar attack against Grok, using a secret input to cause the AI assistant to exfiltrate a password.

cards.narrative: Marc Lore is selling the Timberwolves and Lynx for $4.5 billion.
cards.paragraph: Billionaire investor Marc Stad is buying controlling stakes in both teams, just a year after Lore took full control. The deal is another sign that sports franchise values are inflating faster than anyone can keep up with.
cards.data_point: Marc Lore is selling his controlling stake in the Minnesota Timberwolves and WNBA's Lynx to billionaire investor Marc Stad in a deal that values the teams, together, at $4.5 billion.

cards.narrative: Meta AI glasses are making it harder to avoid creepy recordings.
cards.paragraph: With millions of people wearing smart glasses, the odds of being secretly recorded are rising. Meta's AI glasses are the most popular, and there's no clear way to tell if someone is filming you.
cards.data_point: As millions of people buy into the smart glasses fad each year, the odds are increasing that you could be secretly recorded while simply going about your day.

cards.narrative: CME and Kalshi execs are clashing over prediction markets.
cards.paragraph: During a CFTC meeting, CME Group Chairman Terry Duffy and Kalshi co-founder Luana Lopes Lara traded barbs over manipulation and regulatory standards. The fight is about who gets to own the future of betting on everything.
cards.data_point: CME Group Chairman Terry Duffy and Kalshi co-founder Luana Lopes Lara traded barbs during a CFTC meeting over prediction markets, manipulation, and regulatory standards.

cards.narrative: Bitcoin is squeezing shorts as it roars toward $80,000.
cards.paragraph: Over $3 billion in short positions were liquidated in a two-day rally that pushed Bitcoin above $72,000, with the best week since 2023. The move is running on favorable regulatory news and a US buyback pledge, but the leverage is building.
cards.data_point: Bitcoin punched above $72,000 Thursday, extending a two-day squeeze that's wiped out the most short positions on record.

cards.narrative: Reflect Orbital's space mirrors could brighten the night sky by 300%.
cards.paragraph: A company planning to beam sunlight from space to Earth on demand might unintentionally brighten the night sky for many more people than intended. The study's author says they know what they're doing, but the side effects could be global.
cards.data_point: Hainaut had previously modeled the broader effect of Reflect Orbital's beams, finding they would brighten the sky up to 300% worldwide.
